title: Compatibility: SSAO forces an unused per-frame MSAA depth+stencil copy into the 3D back buffer (several ms per frame on ANGLE/D3D11)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (web export with the official templates, and desktop with `--rendering-driver opengl3_angle`).
- The code paths below are unchanged on `master` (65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704).

### System information

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26340), Godot v4.7.2.stable - Compatibility - Chrome 154.0.8037.98, WebGL 2: `ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (0x00002882) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)`. Desktop native GL: NVIDIA 610.88.

### Issue description

In the Compatibility renderer, enabling SSAO makes every frame copy the **multisampled** main depth+stencil buffer into the 3D back-buffer depth texture, but nothing reads that copy. Under ANGLE/D3D11 (Chrome and Edge on Windows, and `opengl3_angle` on desktop) the multisampled stencil resolve is very slow, so SSAO costs several milliseconds per frame that have nothing to do with SSAO itself.

The chain, per frame:

1. [`rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2771-L2773`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2771-L2773): `if (ssao_enabled) scene_state.used_depth_texture = true;`
2. [`#L2951-L2952`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2951-L2952): that calls `rb->check_backbuffer(...)`, which ends in an unconditional `glCheckFramebufferStatus` even when nothing was (re)created ([`render_scene_buffers_gles3.cpp#L552`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/storage/render_scene_buffers_gles3.cpp#L552)).
3. [`#L2974-L2976`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L2974-L2976): `glBlitFramebuffer(..., GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT | GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT, GL_NEAREST)` from the MSAA fbo into the back-buffer depth texture.

But SSAO is applied in `post_copy`, which reads the internal (resolved) depth, not the back-buffer depth ([`#L3124`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/65e8d16951d6963cb3984c090e45f40d1ba5f704/drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp#L3124)). With no material using `hint_depth_texture`, the copy is dead work. For comparison, Godot's own MSAA resolve later in the same frame blits `COLOR|DEPTH` (0x4100) without stencil.

**Measured with the MRP below** (web release export, Chrome with vsync and the frame rate limit off, 3 alternating rounds, 944x445 canvas):

| Variant | Mean fps | Frame ms |
|---|---|---|
| a. SSAO on, MSAA 4x | 258 | 3.88 |
| b. SSAO off, MSAA 4x | 667 | 1.50 |
| c. SSAO on, stencil bit removed from that one blit (JS shim) | 636 | 1.57 |
| d. SSAO on, MSAA off | 626 | 1.60 |
| e. SSAO on, `glCheckFramebufferStatus` faked, blit kept | 311 | 3.21 |
| f. SSAO on, that blit skipped entirely | 657 | 1.52 |

At 1904x985: a = 97 fps (10.3 ms), b = 481, c = 478, f = 467. So the cost grows with resolution, about 8 ms per frame at 1080p.

- The cost is the multisampled **stencil** resolve. Dropping only the stencil bit (c), or skipping the copy (f), recovers almost everything. Faking the framebuffer check alone (e) does not: the stall then surfaces at the next sync point.
- Single-sampled depth+stencil blits are cheap (d).
- The picture does not change. Screenshots of a vs c and a vs f differ in **0 pixels** (fps label cropped). b differs from a in 188k pixels, so SSAO is visibly active.
- Desktop, 960x540, same project: `opengl3_angle` gives ~285 fps with SSAO on vs ~855 with it off. Native `opengl3` on NVIDIA shows no measurable difference, so this mainly hits ANGLE (that is, most web players on Windows).

We first saw it in a real game's web build: about 5 ms per frame (48.8 to 65.4 fps with the stencil bit removed, 74.3 with SSAO off).

**Possible fixes** (any one helps, the first is the largest):

1. Don't force `used_depth_texture` for SSAO, since post reads the internal depth.
2. When the back-buffer depth copy *is* needed (`hint_depth_texture`), blit `GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT` only. The texture is only ever sampled as depth.
3. In `check_backbuffer`, call `glCheckFramebufferStatus` only when an attachment was (re)created. This one alone is small, about 0.5 ms here.

Workaround for affected web projects: a small JS hook on `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.blitFramebuffer` that clears `STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT` when the read framebuffer's depth-stencil attachment is a multisampled renderbuffer and the draw framebuffer's is a texture.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP and export it for Web (single-threaded), or run it on desktop with `--rendering-driver opengl3_angle`.
2. Run it in Chrome on Windows (ANGLE/D3D11). Optionally start Chrome with `--disable-gpu-vsync --disable-frame-rate-limit` to see uncapped fps.
3. Compare `index.html` with `index.html#ssao=0`. The script polls the hash once a second. On desktop, use `-- ssao=0`. `msaa=0` switches MSAA off.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Three text files (Compatibility, MSAA 4x, SSAO on, 64 meshes, one shadowed directional light):

<details><summary>project.godot</summary>

```ini
config_version=5

[application]
config/name="ssao-backbuffer-mrp"
run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"
config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7", "GL Compatibility")

[display]
window/size/viewport_width=960
window/size/viewport_height=540
window/vsync/vsync_mode=0

[rendering]
renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
renderer/rendering_method.mobile="gl_compatibility"
anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d=2
```
</details>

<details><summary>main.tscn</summary>

```
[gd_scene load_steps=3 format=3]

[ext_resource type="Script" path="res://main.gd" id="1"]

[sub_resource type="Environment" id="env"]
background_mode = 1
background_color = Color(0.35, 0.45, 0.55, 1)
ambient_light_source = 2
ambient_light_color = Color(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 1)
ssao_enabled = true

[node name="Main" type="Node3D"]
script = ExtResource("1")

[node name="WorldEnvironment" type="WorldEnvironment" parent="."]
environment = SubResource("env")

[node name="Camera3D" type="Camera3D" parent="."]

[node name="Sun" type="DirectionalLight3D" parent="."]
shadow_enabled = true

[node name="Label" type="Label" parent="."]
```
</details>

<details><summary>main.gd</summary>

```gdscript
extends Node3D
# Runtime switches, polled once a second so one page load serves every variant:
#   web:     location.hash, e.g. index.html#ssao=0&msaa=0
#   desktop: user args,     e.g. godot --path . -- ssao=0 msaa=0
@onready var env: Environment = $WorldEnvironment.environment
var _opts := "?"
var _t := 1.0

func _ready() -> void:
	$Camera3D.look_at_from_position(Vector3(0, 9, 12), Vector3.ZERO)
	$Sun.rotation_degrees = Vector3(-50, 30, 0)
	var ground := MeshInstance3D.new()
	ground.mesh = PlaneMesh.new()
	ground.mesh.size = Vector2(40, 40)
	add_child(ground)
	for i in 64:
		var m := MeshInstance3D.new()
		m.mesh = BoxMesh.new() if i % 2 == 0 else SphereMesh.new()
		m.position = Vector3(i % 8 - 3.5, 0.5 + (i % 3) * 0.4, floori(i / 8.0) - 3.5) * 1.4
		add_child(m)
	RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time(get_viewport().get_viewport_rid(), true)

func _read_opts() -> String:
	if OS.has_feature("web"):
		return str(JavaScriptBridge.eval("location.hash"))
	return " ".join(OS.get_cmdline_user_args())

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	_t += delta
	if _t < 1.0:
		return
	_t = 0.0
	var opts := _read_opts()
	if opts != _opts:
		_opts = opts
		env.ssao_enabled = not opts.contains("ssao=0")
		get_viewport().msaa_3d = Viewport.MSAA_DISABLED if opts.contains("msaa=0") else Viewport.MSAA_4X
	var vp := get_viewport().get_viewport_rid()
	var line := "fps %d ssao=%s msaa=%d cpu_ms=%.2f gpu_ms=%.2f" % [Engine.get_frames_per_second(),
		env.ssao_enabled, get_viewport().msaa_3d, RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_cpu(vp),
		RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu(vp)]
	$Label.text = line
	print(line)
```
</details>

---
Found while optimizing the web build of [Hex Tower Boogie](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4791970/).
